b2-colombiaandina-01.title: Communicative Challenge: Laws for the Páramos
b2-colombiaandina-01.scenario: You are Meg. You and Carlos are watching a documentary about the páramos of Colombia, and he asks what the environmental groups want.
b2-colombiaandina-01.prompt: Tell Carlos what the environmental groups ask for.
cues: Say that they ask for laws
Say what the laws should do
b2-colombiaandina-01.target: Piden leyes que protejan los páramos.
b2-colombiaandina-01.english: They are asking for laws that protect the páramos.
b2-colombiaandina-01.canDo: I can say what I am looking for or what does not exist with *que* + subjunctive (*Busco un guía que conozca…*).

b2-colombiaandina-02.title: Communicative Challenge: A City at 2,600 Metres
b2-colombiaandina-02.scenario: You are Carlos. You and Meg are planning a trip and reading about Bogotá, and she asks what surprises visitors.
b2-colombiaandina-02.prompt: Tell Meg what surprises many visitors, commenting on the fact.
cues: Mention the height of the city
Say that it surprises many visitors
b2-colombiaandina-02.target: El hecho de que la ciudad esté a 2600 metros sorprende a muchos visitantes.
b2-colombiaandina-02.english: The fact that the city is at 2,600 metres surprises many visitors.
b2-colombiaandina-02.canDo: I can comment on a known fact with *el hecho de que* + subjunctive (Colombia I).

b2-colombiaandina-03.title: Communicative Challenge: The City of Eternal Spring
b2-colombiaandina-03.scenario: You are Meg. You and Carlos are reading an article about Medellín, and he asks whether it is a hot city.
b2-colombiaandina-03.prompt: Correct the idea that Medellín is hot and give the real reason.
cues: Reject the idea that it is hot
Say what its climate is like
b2-colombiaandina-03.target: No es que haga mucho calor, sino que la temperatura casi no cambia.
b2-colombiaandina-03.english: It is not that it is very hot, but that the temperature hardly changes.
b2-colombiaandina-03.canDo: I can reject a reason and give the real one with *no es que* + subjunctive and *sino que* + indicative.

b2-colombiaandina-04.title: Communicative Challenge: Coffee Picked by Hand
b2-colombiaandina-04.scenario: You are Carlos. You and Meg are watching a documentary about the Coffee Cultural Landscape, and she asks how the coffee is harvested.
b2-colombiaandina-04.prompt: Tell Meg how the coffee is harvested.
cues: Say why it is done that way
b2-colombiaandina-04.target: El café se recoge a mano, porque el terreno es difícil.
b2-colombiaandina-04.english: The coffee is picked by hand, because the terrain is difficult.
b2-colombiaandina-04.canDo: I can describe how something is done with the passive *se* (*se recoge*, *se secan*).

b2-colombiaandina-05.title: Communicative Challenge: Where Gabo Began
b2-colombiaandina-05.scenario: You are Meg. You and Carlos are reading about García Márquez, and he asks whether he began as a novelist.
b2-colombiaandina-05.prompt: Correct Carlos with a stance adverb: say how he really began his career.
cues: Use an adverb that corrects an expectation
Say what his first work was
b2-colombiaandina-05.target: En realidad, empezó su carrera como periodista.
b2-colombiaandina-05.english: In fact, he began his career as a journalist.
b2-colombiaandina-05.canDo: I can comment on a fact with a stance adverb such as *en realidad*, *en rigor* or *afortunadamente*.

b2-colombiaandina-consolidation.title: Communicative Challenge: Crops for the Páramo
b2-colombiaandina-consolidation.scenario: You are Carlos. After the unit on the Colombian Andes, Meg asks what the farmers of the páramos need.
b2-colombiaandina-consolidation.prompt: Tell Meg what the farmers of the páramo need.
cues: Say that the crops should not harm the water
b2-colombiaandina-consolidation.target: Los campesinos necesitan cultivos que no dañen el agua del páramo.
b2-colombiaandina-consolidation.english: The farmers need crops that do not harm the water of the páramo.
b2-colombiaandina-consolidation.canDo: I can say what I am looking for or what does not exist with *que* + subjunctive.
